heroHeadline: Reuters Satellite Analysis: Scarborough Shoal Object Disappeared by June 1 — China Silent as Philippines Probe Enters Day 3; Xiang Yang Hong 33 Day 30 Near Pag-asa; Five Simultaneous WPS Pressure Fronts
heroSubtitle: Reuters analysis (June 4) of satellite imagery from Vantor (May 27–30) and SeaLight (May 28) confirmed a small reflective object — consistent with a 'floating raft or buoy' — appeared at Scarborough Shoal's southern lagoon entrance before disappearing from June 1 imagery, suggesting possible removal ahead of scrutiny. The Philippines formally launched an official investigation June 3 (Def. Sec. Teodoro, Gen. Brawner); China has maintained complete silence for three days on both the imagery and diplomatic inquiries — consistent with Beijing's deniable incremental playbook used at Fiery Cross, Subi, and Mischief reefs. As of June 5, five simultaneous West Philippine Sea pressure fronts are active: (1) Scarborough Shoal probe — Day 3, object unconfirmed removed or temporary; (2) Xiang Yang Hong 33 near Pag-asa Island — Day 30, China's UNCLOS Article 246 diplomatic silence reaches Day 25, the longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument under the Marcos administration; (3) Second Thomas Shoal — ongoing CCG blockade of BRP Sierra Madre garrison; (4) China CCG patrols east of Taiwan — response to Japan-Philippines maritime boundary delimitation talks launched May 29; (5) Scarborough Shoal CCG law-enforcement patrols — continuous since PLA STC 'combat readiness patrols' on June 1. AUKUS revised submarine plan (three in-service Virginia-class, announced June 1) and the inaugural Pillar II UUV signature project (deliveries from 2027) remain the primary allied deterrence development of the period.
